# Core decision coverage

## Scope and authority

Reviewed the complete recursively discovered `rework/` tree: **51 artifacts, 30 Markdown sources**. The accepted implementation plan and linked conditional-write evidence are supplemental sources, not silently counted as rework files. This register maps **223 stable decision identities to 112 focused ADRs**. Counts are computed from the register authoring data, not source headings.

All runtime implementation is **unimplemented at D1**. Accepted decisions outside the foundation remain paused. Later explicit amendments control older duplicate summaries. Source paths below are provenance labels, not broken links to ignored files. ADRs contain the decisions and rationale needed without the original notes or scratch plan.

The inventory's hashes identify exactly what was reviewed. Complete bodies, tables, amendments and visual text were read in bounded batches; long physical lines were wrapped for review rather than truncated. HTML presentation CSS was non-decision formatting; all semantic text/links and script contents were inspected. PNG was visually checked as the SVG's rendered counterpart. Probe code/results were read as evidence, not rerun as production tests.

**Reconciliation rule:** only explicitly selected choices (including decisions to defer/reject) become decision identities. Fictional scenario values, audit recommendations, generic external-library comparisons, speculative future alternatives and probe observations remain non-decisions. A section can contain selected restatements and unresolved details together. The occurrence table below maps reviewed statements, not every sentence in that section, to their controlling identity.

**Classification caveat:** no unresolved foundation decision-classification ambiguity was found. Earlier visual-only recommendations and saved future Memory staging details lack independent acceptance evidence; they remain unselected, as their own labels and later Markdown scope notes specify. Their exact possible future contracts are not silently resolved. This documentation does not certify #148/#149 or any runtime backend.

## Source-section reconciliation and duplicate occurrences

These sections partition every Markdown source completely; they are a review ledger, not the decision-count unit. Every explicit controlling Markdown passage in a decision row must map back to that identity in each intersected occurrence section, including historical choices and reversals. Additional reviewed duplicate/restatement occurrences may lie outside those controlling passages. Line partitions and this consistency check do not alone prove exhaustive semantic extraction; exact decisions and source dispositions still require review. Refer to the decision row and ADR for current disposition. Source section headings are descriptive provenance, not links to ignored files.

## Not decisions and unresolved detail boundaries

- **Visual alternatives:** S03's four workflow options and recommended Kanban architecture; S32's independent Question/Slice/Blueprint roots, one-word naming, Evidence-record cardinalities and old Run/Gate/Action sketches; S33's fictional customer-support policies, counts, IDs, concurrency, limits and results; S37's Python/SQLite plugin tree, roadmap, broad dispatch/event/continuous-frontier and idempotent-effect recipes are recommendations/illustrations, not additional accepted implementation requirements. Later explicit portable-Core, ownership, human progression and scope decisions control. No unique visual-only acceptance was inferred.
- **Future Memory publication:** S31's private draft visibility/staging/completion and base-revision/finalization alternatives are saved direction within a selected deferral, not an approved publication algorithm. No finalization action or block-completion policy was selected.
- **Runtime port and bridge details:** exact AgentRuntime signatures/handle storage/injection timing, trusted endpoint transport, malformed/unknown submission errors and recovery matrices remain unfinished. The conceptual openSession/submit/inspect example is not a final interface. The foundation does not invent a placeholder runtime.
- **Repository details:** ref-selector syntax/default branch, provider redirects/moved/reused names, PAT variants/permissions, content provenance and endpoint/error schemas remain unselected. Audit suggestions to pin provider identities or refuse redirects are not adopted here. Generic exact-string and secrecy constraints still apply.
- **Paused domain details:** exact Expedition/Question/Blueprint/AgentInteraction fields, fingerprint/acceptance representation, nested proposal payload/compilation, stale/concurrent command errors, materialized initial Delivery/Slice states, read/handoff schema and final shipped-Expedition closure remain unresolved, not permission to invent fields. The declined Slice-overlap policy remains unselected; the static-directory mutation-serialization constraint is narrower.
- **Research and probes:** S05–S17 counterexamples, compiler fixtures and synthetic values are evidence only. Persistent adapters were not qualified by these reports, and a passing defect assertion is not a fix. S27 describes original Core rather than selecting a no-classes rule. S40's library/contract/query proposals, S47's SQL SDK comparisons and advanced migration ideas, S50/S51's external framework precedents are not automatic domain policy. Only recorded subsequent selections are mapped.
- **Core version-schema proposal:** S35:174 and S25:9,99 distinguish the earlier selected last-version-only policy (MIG-H01) from the proposed new Core-owned version schema. That concrete mechanism was not adopted; its single-marker transaction probe is supporting evidence about a rejected alternative, not a superseded accepted model. Native ledger adoption controls. Numeric progression history is recorded separately as MIG-H03.
- **Rejected/unselected refinements:** runtime Repo/builder facade, callback reentry tracking, relational output predicates, explicit codec round-trip machinery, public raw handlers, identity-only resolver restrictions, no-op equality checks, arbitrary local-key proposal DAGs, forced extra intake/Destination gates and template placeholder work are not required. Their controlling ADRs preserve why the selected alternative wins.

## Mechanical verification contract

Check the live inventory against this table and its hashes; all sources must have a completed review disposition. Check unique decision keys, existing ADR files/anchors, allowed status values, every ADR indexed, every historical replacement reciprocal, distinct original and supersession rationale, complete Markdown section partitions, every controlling Markdown provenance range against occurrence membership (including historical choices), register/ADR provenance agreement, and all relative links. Tighten overly broad citations rather than mapping unrelated decisions to entire sources. Exact runtime behavior is verified later by implementation tasks, never by this register. D1 must leave source, manifests, lockfile, original notes and existing docs/core untouched.
